archetypes.name: contract-drift
archetypes.rationale: The plan asserts wait-for-reviewers.sh always exits 0 yet the dispatch-code-voters.sh snippet checks _wait_rc != 0, making the warning path dead code — one of these claims is wrong.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit every place the plan relies on a documented exit-code or return-value contract from an existing script. Cross-reference the plan's stated contract against the actual script files: for wait-for-reviewers.sh the plan's Edge Cases section says 'exits 0 for normal operation including timeouts' but the injected code uses set +e and (( _wait_rc != 0 )) with a larch_err warning — if the script truly always exits 0, the warning branch is dead code and the set +e guard is misleading. Also flag any place where the plan's own prose contradicts itself on the same mechanism (e.g., 'exits 0 on timeout' vs 'if wait-for-reviewers.sh returns non-zero (timeout), do NOT abort' in the Failure Modes section). Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: impl-method-conflict
archetypes.rationale: The plan prescribes two mutually incompatible implementation patterns for the Codex stdin redirect in the same file: modifying the _launch_capture_stdout_only helper and using inline case statements — an implementer cannot satisfy both simultaneously.
archetypes.prompt_body: Identify every place the plan describes the same code change in two or more ways that cannot both be true. Specifically, the run-external-agent.sh Changes section says 'modify _launch_capture_stdout_only to accept (or inherit) the stdin policy and apply < /dev/null for Codex spawns' while the Implementation Approach section says 'use "$@" < /dev/null directly inside a case "$TOOL_NAME" in codex) ... ;; esac per-branch, not via a string variable' — these prescribe different code structures for the CAPTURE_STDOUT_ONLY branch. Flag which pattern is authoritative, whether the chosen pattern actually covers all three spawn branches without ambiguity, and whether the plan's acceptance criteria ('all three background spawn branches') are achievable with the described approach. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: test-probe-validity
archetypes.rationale: The Codex stdin probe test uses $$ (the stub script's own PID) to inspect fd 0, which reads the stub's stdin rather than the spawned Codex subprocess's stdin and would pass trivially even without the fix.
archetypes.prompt_body: For each new test case described in the plan, verify that the validation mechanism actually exercises the described failure mode rather than passing trivially. The 'Codex stdin redirect' test uses lsof -p $$ or readlink /proc/$$/fd/0 inside the stub binary — $$ is the stub's own shell PID, not the PID of the Codex subprocess launched by run-external-agent.sh, so the probe reads the wrong process's fd 0. Also check whether test-run-external-agent.sh appears in the Files to modify/create list (the Testing Strategy section references it as a required pass but it may be absent from the file list). Finally check whether the 'assert dispatcher waits properly via timestamp comparison' mechanism is specified precisely enough to be implemented without ambiguity. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
